newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers to discuss east Zaire crisis.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers to discuss east Zaire crisis.

text.p: European Union development ministers meet in Brussels on Thursday to discuss aid for refugees scattered across eastern Zaire, but will avoid serious discussion on whether to intervene militarily to deliver it.

EU sources say the meeting will examine proposals by humanitarian aid chief Emma Bonino to deliver food to the region by setting up "safe corridors" across the Great Lakes region of Burundi, Rwanda and Zaire.

"Thursday's meeting will result in significant pledges of EU and bilateral aid," a Belgian foreign ministry source said. But he said details of any corridors and, more importantly, how to police them effectively, had yet to be worked out.

The 15-nation EU has offered to help create and finance an African force, but seven regional leaders meeting in Nairobi on Tuesday said they wanted the United Nations to create a "neutral force" to come to the rescue of the refugees.
France and Spain have suggested sending an international force but the rest of the world, including Europe and the United States, are uninterested in any African adventures.

Aldo Ajello, the EU's special envoy to the Great Lakes region, is likely to brief the meeting on his latest trip to the area -- one of a series in a diplomatic ballet which has so far produced only meetings.
